title: Unit-Aware Differentially Private Quantum Machine Learning for Clinical and Wearable Health Data
abstract: arXiv:2610.28968v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Clinical registries and wearable sensors support early health-risk assessment, yet models trained on these records may leak sensitive information when released. Differential privacy (DP) bounds this leakage by injecting noise whose total magnitude grows with the number of trainable parameters, a cost especially severe for small health cohorts. This motivates parameter efficient models including quantum machine learning (QML), whose variational circuits can represent complex decision boundaries with few trainable parameters. It raises a question: at matched input dimensionality and privacy budget, does a quantum model retain more utility than a classical one? We investigate this question on three clinical cohorts and one wearable cohort, treating each clinical record or participant as a privacy unit. translated_title: 面向临床与可穿戴健康数据的单元感知差分隐私量子机器学习
translated_abstract: 临床登记数据和可穿戴传感器可支持早期健康风险评估，但基于这些记录训练的模型在发布时可能泄露敏感信息。差分隐私（DP）通过注入噪声来限制这种泄露，而噪声的总幅度会随可训练参数数量的增加而增长，这一代价对规模较小的健康队列尤为严重。这促使人们关注参数高效的模型，包括量子机器学习（QML），其变分电路能够以少量可训练参数表达复杂的决策边界。由此引出一个问题：在输入维度与隐私预算匹配的情况下，量子模型是否比经典模型保留更多效用？我们在三个临床队列和一个可穿戴设备队列上研究这一问题，将每条临床记录或每位参与者视为一个隐私单元，并在五种隐私预算和五个随机种子下，对容量匹配的量子模型、多层感知机和逻辑回归模型进行了比较。（注：原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种“单元感知”的差分隐私量子机器学习方法，将每条临床记录或每位可穿戴设备用户视为隐私单元，并在输入维度、隐私预算与模型容量匹配的条件下与经典模型对比，以检验可训练参数更少的量子模型能否在保护隐私的同时为临床与健康数据保留更多预测效用。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a unit-aware differentially private quantum machine learning approach that treats each clinical record or wearable participant as a privacy unit and compares capacity-matched quantum and classical models under matched input dimensionality and privacy budgets, testing whether the parameter-efficient quantum model retains more utility for private clinical and wearable health prediction.
